title: Canonical coefficient identifications and finite projections of immersion pullback
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbb Q_\ell$, its integral adic datum $d$, schemes $X,Y$ and $f:Y\to X$. Quotient representatives determine unique finite coefficient identifications; compatibility with every finite projection determines the completed coefficient identification. Ordinary resolving pullback is canonically isomorphic to exact termwise inverse image, with its original universal counit. The finite tensor comparisons respect scalar-extension units, every quotient transition and quotient composition. Under derived tower evaluation, every finite projection of completed pullback carries the specified completion unit to pullback of the finite scalar unit; the projections respect all quotient transitions. The attached declarations are the original coefficient, ordinary, finite comparison and projection constructions of the parent node.

proof.text: Quotient induction supplies the unique quotientEquiv on the specified representatives. IntegralCoefficientPresentation.comparison supplies completedRingIso with its unique finite projection equations. Identify actual and normalized module pullback; uniqueness of the universal left-derived pair gives derivedIso with the counit equation.

Apply the existing generic finite-comparison normalization to the integral adic datum. Its scalar unit equation, transition equation and quotient cocycle give finite_compatibility. The specified strict tower evaluation identifies each level with the restricted scalar reduction.

For completedProjection_compatibility, evaluate the constant/limit counit on the pulled reduction augmentation. The adjunction triangle identity identifies the finite projection. Apply the normalized K-flat augmentation-unit equation and descend by naturality. For transitions use the derived-limit projection transition equation, ExactTowerAugmentedCounit.interchange_transition and the generic evaluation transition equation, then cancel the finite evaluation isomorphisms.
